rules.name: sdk-must-not-import-plugins
rules.why: The SDK is public surface for plugin authors and is source-agnostic. If it can import a plugin, every collector inherits that plugin's dependencies and the SDK stops being something a third party can build against alone.

rules.name: sdk-must-not-import-source-clients
rules.why: The SDK is source-agnostic. A source client here would put a Keycloak dependency in the build of every plugin anyone ever writes.

rules.name: contract-module-stays-standalone
rules.why: api/ holds generated contract types. Every collector depends on it, so it must depend on nothing of ours.

rules.name: tools-are-standalone
rules.why: Build tooling must not depend on shipped code, or a broken build becomes a broken linter and the failure is unreadable.

rules.name: plugin-keycloak-does-not-import-other-plugins
rules.why: Each collector is its own module and its own binary. If one imports another, a buyer auditing the Keycloak collector is auditing the GitHub one too, and the two can no longer be released apart. A new collector adds a rule here.
